Consolidated billing is the AWS Organizations feature that merges all member account charges into a single invoice issued to the management account. It also pools usage from all accounts when calculating volume-based pricing tiers, which can reduce per-unit costs for services like Amazon S3.

**Why it works:** By aggregating usage across all linked accounts, consolidated billing ensures the organization benefits from volume discounts that individual accounts might not reach on their own, while simplifying invoice management.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Service control policies: govern permissions, not billing or pricing.
- Cost Allocation Tags: organize cost data within reports; they do not consolidate invoices or affect pricing tiers.
- AWS Budgets: monitors spending thresholds; it does not change how invoices are structured or how usage is aggregated for pricing.

skills: 4.2.3: Understanding AWS Organizations consolidated billing and allocation of costs.
questions.question:
Following a board decision to consolidate cloud spending across business units, the company's cloud team has enabled AWS Organizations with consolidated billing. The operations team is asked to explain the benefits the organization will gain from this change.

Which TWO benefits does consolidated billing in AWS Organizations provide?

choices.text: A single monthly invoice for all member accounts, issued to the management account.
choices.explanation: Consolidated billing combines all member account charges into one invoice for the management account, replacing multiple separate invoices.

choices.text: Aggregated usage across all member accounts, which can qualify the organization for volume pricing discounts on eligible services.
choices.explanation: By pooling usage from all accounts, consolidated billing allows the organization to reach higher usage tiers faster, reducing per-unit costs on services such as Amazon S3 and AWS Data Transfer.

choices.text: Automatic enforcement of spending limits on member accounts so no individual account can exceed its allocated budget.
choices.explanation: Consolidated billing does not enforce spending limits or budget caps on member accounts. Budget enforcement requires AWS Budgets with budget actions or service control policies.

choices.text: Automatic deletion of underutilized resources in member accounts to reduce costs across the organization.
choices.explanation: Consolidated billing has no resource management or cleanup capability. Identifying underutilized resources requires AWS Trusted Advisor or AWS Cost Explorer.

choices.text: Centralized IAM permission management across all member accounts, replacing per-account identity configurations.
choices.explanation: Consolidated billing does not affect IAM policies or identity management. Cross-account permission management is handled through IAM roles, AWS Organizations SCPs, or AWS IAM Identity Center.

questions.tip: Focus on the financial and invoicing benefits that consolidation directly introduces, not on capabilities that belong to other services.
questions.explanation:
Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations provides two direct financial benefits: a single invoice to the management account and aggregated usage that can unlock volume pricing tiers across the organization.

**Why they work:** These are core, documented features of consolidated billing - invoice consolidation simplifies payment, and usage pooling can reduce per-unit charges on tiered services.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Spending limits on member accounts: requires AWS Budgets with actions or SCPs, not consolidated billing itself.
- Automatic resource deletion: no AWS service deletes resources automatically based on billing data.
- Centralized IAM management: handled by IAM, SCPs, or AWS IAM Identity Center, not by billing consolidation.

skills: 4.2.4: Understanding various types of cost allocation tags and their relation to billing reports (for example, AWS Cost and Usage Report).
questions.question:
The operations team has been tagging Amazon EC2 instances with a key named `Project` and value names corresponding to internal project codes. After a month of tagging, the finance team reports they cannot see any `Project` breakdown in the Cost and Usage Report.

What step is required before cost allocation tags appear as columns in the Cost and Usage Report?

choices.text: The `Project` tag key must be activated as a cost allocation tag in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console before it will appear as a column in the Cost and Usage Report.
choices.explanation: Tags applied to resources do not automatically appear in billing reports. Each tag key must be explicitly activated as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console, after which it will show as a column in future Cost and Usage Reports.

choices.text: The tag must be added to every resource in the account using the AWS Tag Editor, then the Cost and Usage Report will automatically detect and include it.
choices.explanation: Applying a tag to more resources does not cause it to appear in billing reports. Activation in the Billing console is the required step, regardless of how many resources carry the tag.

choices.text: The Cost and Usage Report must be deleted and re-created with a new configuration that includes a list of tag keys to expose in the report.
choices.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports do not require re-creation to include new tag columns. Once a tag is activated as a cost allocation tag, it automatically appears in subsequent report deliveries.

choices.text: An IAM policy granting `ce:GetTags` must be attached to the billing role so the Cost Explorer service can surface the tag data in the report.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions for `ce:GetTags` control access to tag data within Cost Explorer, not the activation of cost allocation tags in billing reports. These are separate concepts and separate consoles.

questions.tip: Consider the specific activation step that makes a resource tag visible as a filterable dimension in billing reports.
questions.explanation:
Resource tags do not automatically flow into billing reports. To appear as a column in the Cost and Usage Report, a tag key must first be activated as a cost allocation tag in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console under the Cost Allocation Tags section.

**Why it works:** Activation signals to the billing system that this tag key should be tracked and included as a dimension in future report exports, starting from the date of activation.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Using Tag Editor to apply the tag broadly: tag coverage on resources has no effect on report columns without activation.
- Deleting and re-creating the report: report configuration does not include a tag allowlist; activation is handled separately.
- Attaching an IAM policy for `ce:GetTags`: this controls API access to tag data in Cost Explorer, not whether tags appear in billing reports.

skills: 4.2.4: Understanding various types of cost allocation tags and their relation to billing reports (for example, AWS Cost and Usage Report).
questions.question: Match each cost allocation tagging scenario to the correct outcome or behavior.

slots.label: A customer applies the tag `Environment: Production` to an Amazon EC2 instance but does not activate it in the Billing console.
A customer activates the `Team` tag key in the Billing console and it appears as a column in the Cost and Usage Report.
AWS automatically applies the tag `aws:cloudformation:stack-name` to resources launched by an AWS CloudFormation stack.

choices.text: The tag exists on the resource but will not appear as a cost dimension in billing reports.
choices.explanation: Tags must be activated as cost allocation tags before they appear in billing reports. Simply applying a tag to a resource has no effect on billing visibility.

choices.text: Each resource tagged with the Team key will have its costs grouped under the corresponding tag value in the report.
choices.explanation: Once a tag key is activated, the Cost and Usage Report includes it as a column, and costs for tagged resources are attributed to the corresponding tag value for filtering and allocation.

choices.text: This is an AWS-generated tag with the reserved aws: prefix, created automatically without customer action.
choices.explanation: AWS-generated tags use the reserved aws: prefix and are created by AWS services like CloudFormation automatically. Customers can activate them in the Billing console but cannot create or modify tags with this prefix.

questions.tip: Consider the activation requirement, what activated tags enable, and which tag type is created automatically by AWS services.
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags require explicit activation in the AWS Billing console to appear in billing reports, regardless of whether they exist on resources. Once activated, each tagged resource's costs are grouped by the tag value in the Cost and Usage Report. AWS-generated tags like those from CloudFormation are created automatically using the reserved `aws:` prefix and can be activated separately from user-defined tags.

skills: 4.3.1: Locating AWS whitepapers, blogs, and documentation on official AWS websites.
questions.question:
During a cloud adoption planning session, a developer wants to read detailed technical walkthroughs, announcements of new AWS features, and practical implementation examples written by AWS engineers and solutions architects. They specifically want content that is regularly updated as new services launch.

Which official AWS online resource BEST satisfies this need?

choices.text: The AWS News Blog at aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws, where AWS publishes feature announcements, deep dives, and implementation walkthroughs authored by AWS teams
choices.explanation: The AWS News Blog (and associated AWS Blogs network) is the primary channel where AWS publishes regular technical content, service announcements, and implementation guides.

choices.text: AWS re:Invent session recordings on YouTube, which contain presentation slides and live demos from the annual conference
choices.explanation: re:Invent recordings are useful but are event-specific and not regularly updated; they are hosted on third-party platforms, not the official AWS blog.

choices.text: The AWS Well-Architected Framework PDF download, which provides static architecture guidance across the six pillars
choices.explanation: The Well-Architected Framework is valuable guidance but is a static framework document, not a regularly updated blog with feature announcements.

choices.text: Third-party cloud comparison sites that aggregate AWS feature release notes alongside those of other cloud providers
choices.explanation: Third-party comparison sites are not official AWS resources and do not contain authoritative AWS-authored content.

questions.tip: Consider the type of resource that publishes ongoing, regularly updated technical content directly from AWS teams.
questions.explanation:
The AWS News Blog and the broader AWS Blogs network at aws.amazon.com/blogs is the official channel for AWS-authored feature announcements, deep dives, and technical walkthroughs that are continuously updated as new services launch.

**Why it works:** AWS blog posts are written by AWS engineers, solutions architects, and service teams, providing timely and authoritative technical content aligned with the current state of AWS services.

**Why the others don't work:**
- re:Invent recordings: Event-specific, not continuously updated, hosted externally.
- Well-Architected Framework PDF: Static framework document, not a regularly updated content channel.
- Third-party comparison sites: Not official AWS resources.

skills: 4.3.2: Identifying and locating AWS technical resources (for example, AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post).
questions.question:
The operations team is troubleshooting an intermittent connectivity issue with their Amazon VPC. They want to search a resource that combines peer-reviewed answers from AWS experts and community members, curated technical articles, and official AWS responses in a single searchable portal.

Which AWS technical resource provides this combination of community and expert answers in one place?

choices.text: AWS re:Post, the community platform that consolidates expert-reviewed answers, technical articles, and community Q&A for AWS services
choices.explanation: AWS re:Post replaced the old AWS Forums and combines peer Q&A with expert-reviewed content and curated knowledge articles in a single searchable portal.

choices.text: AWS Prescriptive Guidance, which publishes step-by-step migration and modernization patterns authored by AWS strategy teams
choices.explanation: AWS Prescriptive Guidance provides migration and modernization strategies but is not a community Q&A platform.

choices.text: The AWS Documentation portal at docs.aws.amazon.com, which contains official API references and service user guides

choices.text: AWS Artifact, the self-service portal for downloading AWS compliance reports and security certifications on demand
choices.explanation: AWS Artifact is a compliance document repository, not a technical Q&A or knowledge resource.

questions.tip: Think about which resource was specifically designed to replace the old AWS Forums with a modern community and expert knowledge platform.
questions.explanation:
AWS re:Post is the official AWS community platform that replaced the former AWS Discussion Forums. It aggregates community Q&A, expert-reviewed answers, and curated technical articles in a single searchable interface.

**Why it works:** re:Post is purpose-built to surface vetted technical answers alongside community discussion, making it ideal for troubleshooting service-specific issues.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Strategy and migration pattern content, not a Q&A community platform.
- AWS Documentation portal: Official service documentation only, no community contributions.
- AWS Artifact: Compliance and audit document repository, unrelated to technical knowledge sharing.

skills: 4.3.2: Identifying and locating AWS technical resources (for example, AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post).
questions.question:
To reduce infrastructure costs, an architect is planning a large-scale migration of legacy on-premises applications to AWS. They need prescriptive, step-by-step strategies that cover migration patterns, tools, and modernization approaches vetted by AWS professional teams.

Which AWS resource provides this type of structured, strategy-level migration and modernization guidance?

choices.text: AWS Prescriptive Guidance, which provides curated strategies, guides, and patterns for migration, modernization, and cloud operations developed by AWS experts
choices.explanation: AWS Prescriptive Guidance publishes prescriptive migration and modernization content covering patterns, tools, and strategies developed and vetted by AWS professional services teams.

choices.text: The AWS Knowledge Center, which contains answers to the most frequently asked technical support questions submitted by AWS customers
choices.explanation: The AWS Knowledge Center addresses common support questions but does not provide comprehensive migration strategy patterns.

choices.text: AWS re:Post, which allows customers and AWS experts to ask and answer technical questions about AWS services in a community forum format
choices.explanation: AWS re:Post is a community Q&A platform, not a structured repository of migration strategies.

choices.text: The AWS Solutions Library, which provides vetted reference architectures and deployable solutions for common workload patterns
choices.explanation: The AWS Solutions Library provides reference architectures and deployable solutions, but AWS Prescriptive Guidance is specifically focused on migration and modernization strategies and patterns.

questions.tip: Consider which resource is purpose-built for step-by-step migration and modernization strategies rather than reference architectures or community answers.
questions.explanation:
AWS Prescriptive Guidance is specifically designed to provide structured, expert-vetted strategies and patterns for migrating and modernizing workloads on AWS.

**Why it works:** Developed by AWS professional services teams, it covers migration patterns, tooling recommendations, and modernization approaches in a structured, actionable format.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Knowledge Center: Addresses common support questions, not comprehensive migration strategies.
- AWS re:Post: Community Q&A platform, not prescriptive migration guidance.
- AWS Solutions Library: Reference architectures and deployable templates, distinct from migration strategy patterns.

skills: 4.3.2: Identifying and locating AWS technical resources (for example, AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post).

AWS Prescriptive Guidance
AWS re:Post

skills: 4.3.3: Identifying AWS Support options for AWS customers (for example, customer service and communities, AWS Developer Support, AWS Business Support, AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support, AWS Enterprise Support).
questions.question:
Management has decided that the company's growing AWS footprint requires a dedicated Technical Account Manager who provides proactive guidance, coordinates access to programs and subject matter experts, and participates in regular operational reviews. The business runs mission-critical workloads where a response time of 15 minutes or less is required for business-critical system failures.

Which AWS Support plan includes a designated Technical Account Manager and the required response SLA?

choices.text: AWS Enterprise Support, which includes a designated Technical Account Manager, proactive guidance, and a less than 15-minute response time for business-critical system-down cases
choices.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support provides a designated TAM and a less than 15-minute response SLA for business-critical system failures, meeting both requirements.

choices.text: AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support, which provides access to a pool of Technical Account Managers on a shared basis and a less than 30-minute response time for business-critical system-down cases
choices.explanation: Enterprise On-Ramp provides shared TAM access rather than a dedicated TAM, and its critical response SLA is 30 minutes rather than 15.

choices.text: AWS Business Support, which provides 24/7 Cloud Support Engineer access and a less than one-hour response time for production system-down cases but does not include a Technical Account Manager
choices.explanation: AWS Business Support does not include a Technical Account Manager and offers a slower response SLA than required.

choices.text: AWS Developer Support, which provides access to a Technical Account Manager during business hours and a general guidance response time of less than 24 hours
choices.explanation: AWS Developer Support does not include a Technical Account Manager at any level and has no sub-one-hour critical response SLA.

questions.tip: Focus on which plan includes a designated, named individual as a proactive support contact rather than shared or pooled access.
questions.explanation:
AWS Enterprise Support is the only plan that includes a designated Technical Account Manager and a less than 15-minute response SLA for business-critical system failures.

**Why it works:** Enterprise Support provides dedicated TAM engagement and the strictest response SLAs available in the AWS Support plan hierarchy.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Enterprise On-Ramp: Shared TAM pool, not a dedicated TAM; 30-minute critical response SLA.
- Business Support: No TAM included; one-hour production-down SLA.
- Developer Support: No TAM; business-hours email access only.

skills: 4.3.3: Identifying AWS Support options for AWS customers (for example, customer service and communities, AWS Developer Support, AWS Business Support, AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support, AWS Enterprise Support).
questions.question:
Following a board decision to formalize their AWS support strategy, the cloud team is reviewing the AWS Support plan tiers. They want to confirm which specific capabilities are available exclusively in the AWS Enterprise Support plan and are NOT included in the AWS Business Support plan.

Which TWO capabilities are exclusive to AWS Enterprise Support and are not available with AWS Business Support?

choices.text: A designated Technical Account Manager who provides proactive guidance, coordinates access to subject matter experts, and leads regular operational reviews
choices.explanation: A designated TAM is exclusive to AWS Enterprise Support; Business Support has no TAM.

choices.text: Access to the AWS Support API to programmatically manage support cases and retrieve Trusted Advisor check results
choices.explanation: AWS Support API access is included in Business Support, not exclusive to Enterprise Support.

choices.text: A less than 15-minute response time for business-critical system-down support cases
choices.explanation: The 15-minute critical response SLA is exclusive to Enterprise Support; Business Support offers a less than one-hour SLA for production-down cases.

choices.text: 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone, chat, and email for production system impairments
choices.explanation: 24/7 Cloud Support Engineer access is included in both Business Support and Enterprise Support.

choices.text: Access to all AWS Trusted Advisor checks and recommendations across cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits
choices.explanation: Full Trusted Advisor check access is available in Business Support, not exclusive to Enterprise Support.

questions.tip: Consider the capabilities that distinguish the highest-tier plan from the second-highest tier, focusing on dedicated human engagement and response time commitments.
questions.explanation:
The two capabilities exclusive to AWS Enterprise Support (not available in Business Support) are a designated Technical Account Manager and the less than 15-minute response SLA for business-critical system-down cases.

**Why they work:** These features are specifically listed as Enterprise-only differentiators in the AWS Support plan comparison.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Support API access: Available in Business Support and above.
- 24/7 Cloud Support Engineer access: Available from Business Support onward.
- Full Trusted Advisor checks: Available starting at Business Support.

skills: 4.3.4: Identifying the role of Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, and the AWS Health API to help manage and monitor environments for cost optimization.
questions.question:
After reviewing quarterly spending, a cloud financial team notices their AWS bill has grown significantly over the past three months. They want a tool that automatically analyzes their AWS environment and surfaces actionable recommendations to reduce costs, including identifying idle Amazon EC2 instances, underutilized Amazon EBS volumes, and unassociated Elastic IP addresses.

Which AWS tool is specifically designed to provide these types of cost optimization recommendations?

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor, which continuously evaluates the AWS environment against best practices and provides recommendations across cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits
choices.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor automatically checks the AWS environment for cost optimization opportunities, including idle resources and underutilized assets.

choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer, which provides interactive graphs and forecasting for analyzing historical spend and usage trends across AWS accounts
choices.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer is an analytics tool for visualizing and forecasting spend, not a proactive best-practice recommendation engine.

choices.text: The AWS Health Dashboard, which displays real-time status of AWS services and provides notifications about events that may affect the customer's specific resources
choices.explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard focuses on service health and event notifications, not cost optimization recommendations.

choices.text: AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes Amazon EC2 instance metrics and recommends optimal instance types based on workload utilization data
choices.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer focuses specifically on instance type right-sizing recommendations, not the broad range of cost optimization checks that Trusted Advisor covers.

questions.tip: Think about the tool that provides a broad set of automated best-practice checks across multiple categories including cost, rather than a single-purpose analytics or sizing tool.
questions.explanation:
AWS Trusted Advisor is designed to evaluate the AWS environment against AWS best practices and surface recommendations across five categories, with cost optimization being one of them.

**Why it works:** Trusted Advisor checks for idle EC2 instances, underutilized EBS volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs, and other cost inefficiencies automatically.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Cost Explorer: Visualizes historical and forecasted spend but does not proactively identify idle resources.
- AWS Health Dashboard: Service health and event notifications, not cost optimization.
- AWS Compute Optimizer: Narrows to right-sizing EC2 instances, not the full breadth of cost optimization checks.

skills: 4.3.4: Identifying the role of Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, and the AWS Health API to help manage and monitor environments for cost optimization.
questions.question:
The operations team is building an automated incident response system. When AWS announces scheduled maintenance or detects an issue affecting specific resources in the company's account, the team wants the system to automatically open a ticket in their internal ITSM tool without requiring manual monitoring of any web console.

Which AWS capability enables this programmatic, account-specific event integration?

choices.text: The AWS Health API, which provides programmatic access to account-specific service health events and scheduled maintenance notifications so they can be ingested by external systems
choices.explanation: The AWS Health API allows applications to retrieve account-specific health events programmatically, enabling automated integration with external systems such as ITSM tools.

choices.text: The AWS Health Dashboard personal view, which displays account-specific health events in the AWS Management Console and can be bookmarked for daily review
choices.explanation: The personal view of the Health Dashboard requires manual console review and does not support automated programmatic integration.

choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch Events rules configured to trigger on AWS service status changes published to the AWS Service Health Dashboard
choices.explanation: The AWS Service Health Dashboard covers general regional status, not account-specific resource events; CloudWatch Events cannot substitute for the AWS Health API for account-specific notifications.

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor notifications configured via Amazon SNS to alert on best-practice deviations detected in the account
choices.explanation: Trusted Advisor SNS notifications cover best-practice check alerts, not scheduled maintenance or service health events affecting specific account resources.

questions.tip: Consider which feature provides programmatic, account-specific health data rather than requiring console access or covering general service availability.
questions.explanation:
The AWS Health API provides programmatic access to account-specific health events, including service disruptions and scheduled maintenance notices that affect the customer's own resources.

**Why it works:** The API returns JSON responses that can be consumed by automation pipelines, enabling ticket creation in ITSM tools without human intervention.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Health Dashboard personal view: Console-only, requires manual monitoring.
- CloudWatch Events with Service Health Dashboard: General regional status, not account-specific resource events.
- Trusted Advisor SNS: Best-practice check alerts, not health event notifications.

skills: 4.3.4: Identifying the role of Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, and the AWS Health API to help manage and monitor environments for cost optimization.

skills: 4.3.5: Identifying the role of the AWS Trust and Safety team to report abuse of AWS resources.
questions.question:
A systems administrator receives an influx of spam emails and confirms that the sending mail servers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in another customer's AWS account. The administrator wants to report this to AWS so the appropriate team can investigate and take corrective action.

Which description BEST characterizes the role of the AWS Trust and Safety team in this scenario?

choices.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team investigates reports of AWS resources being used for abusive activities such as spam, phishing, malware, or DDoS, and takes action against accounts that violate the AWS Acceptable Use Policy
choices.explanation: Trust and Safety is the AWS team responsible for investigating policy violations and abuse reports, including spam originating from EC2 instances, and enforcing the AWS Acceptable Use Policy.

choices.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team provides real-time threat intelligence feeds that customers can subscribe to in order to automatically block IP addresses associated with known abusive AWS resources
choices.explanation: The Trust and Safety team investigates abuse reports; it does not operate a customer-facing threat intelligence feed service.

choices.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team monitors all customer email traffic sent through Amazon SES and automatically quarantines messages identified as spam before they reach external recipients
choices.explanation: Trust and Safety responds to abuse reports; it does not proactively monitor or intercept customer email traffic.

choices.text: The AWS Trust and Safety team issues public advisories identifying AWS customer accounts engaged in abusive behavior so that affected parties can take their own protective measures
choices.explanation: AWS does not publish customer account information publicly; Trust and Safety handles abuse investigation and enforcement privately.

questions.tip: Focus on the investigative and enforcement role this team plays when AWS resources are used in violation of AWS policies.
questions.explanation:
The AWS Trust and Safety team is responsible for receiving abuse reports, investigating violations of the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, and taking appropriate enforcement action against accounts found to be conducting abusive activities.

**Why it works:** When spam, phishing, or other abuse originates from AWS infrastructure, Trust and Safety has the authority to investigate and act on the offending account.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Threat intelligence feeds: Not a function of the Trust and Safety team.
- Proactive email monitoring: Trust and Safety responds to reports, it does not intercept customer email.
- Public advisories: AWS does not publicly identify customer accounts; enforcement is handled confidentially.

skills: 4.3.5: Identifying the role of the AWS Trust and Safety team to report abuse of AWS resources.
questions.question: A network engineer has identified that an AWS-hosted IP address is conducting a port scan against their corporate network. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to properly report this abuse to AWS.

choices.text: Gather evidence including the offending IP addresses, timestamps, log excerpts, and a description of the abusive behavior
choices.explanation: Collecting evidence first ensures the report contains the information Trust and Safety needs to investigate the incident effectively.

choices.text: Navigate to the AWS abuse report form at aws.amazon.com/forms/report-abuse
choices.explanation: After preparing evidence, the engineer accesses the official AWS Trust and Safety abuse reporting form.

choices.text: Complete the form by selecting the abuse category, providing the offending IP addresses, and attaching or pasting the collected evidence
choices.explanation: Filling in the form with the abuse type, offending details, and supporting evidence allows Trust and Safety to route and investigate the report.

choices.text: Submit the report and await a response from the AWS Trust and Safety team with investigation updates or remediation confirmation
choices.explanation: Submitting the completed form sends it to the Trust and Safety team, who will follow up as they investigate and take action.

questions.tip: Think about what information needs to be ready before accessing the reporting channel, and what happens after the form is submitted.
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is to gather evidence, navigate to the AWS abuse report form, complete it with all required details, and then submit it to the Trust and Safety team. Collecting evidence before filling out the form ensures a complete and actionable report.

skills: 4.3.6: Understanding the role of AWS Partners (for example, AWS Marketplace, independent software vendors, system integrators).
questions.question:
The organization is looking to deploy a third-party security information and event management solution on AWS. Rather than procuring and licensing the software separately through a vendor's sales team, the team wants to find, evaluate, and purchase pre-configured software that deploys directly into their AWS account with consolidated billing through their existing AWS invoice.

Which AWS partner resource should they use?

choices.text: AWS Marketplace, a digital catalog where third-party independent software vendors list products that customers can evaluate, subscribe to, and deploy directly into their AWS account with charges appearing on their AWS bill
choices.explanation: AWS Marketplace allows customers to find, subscribe to, and deploy third-party software with billing consolidated into their AWS invoice, eliminating separate vendor procurement.

choices.text: The AWS Partner Network directory, where customers can browse certified AWS Partners and contact them directly to arrange custom software licensing agreements
choices.explanation: The APN directory helps customers find partner companies; it is not a procurement or deployment platform and does not consolidate billing into the AWS invoice.

choices.text: AWS Service Catalog, which allows organizations to create and manage approved catalogs of AWS services and configurations for internal use within their own account
choices.explanation: AWS Service Catalog manages internally approved product portfolios; it is not a marketplace for discovering and purchasing third-party software from external vendors.

choices.text: AWS OpsWorks, which provides managed instances of Chef and Puppet for automating server configuration and can deploy community cookbooks from public repositories
choices.explanation: AWS OpsWorks is a configuration management service; it is not a software procurement or discovery platform.

questions.tip: Think about which platform combines software discovery, procurement, deployment, and consolidated AWS billing in a single experience.
questions.explanation:
AWS Marketplace is the digital catalog that enables customers to find, evaluate, and purchase third-party software with billing consolidated directly into their AWS invoice.

**Why it works:** AWS Marketplace integrates the full procurement lifecycle - discovery, subscription, deployment, and billing - without requiring a separate vendor relationship.

**Why the others don't work:**
- APN directory: Partner discovery only, no integrated procurement or billing.
- AWS Service Catalog: Manages internal product portfolios, not external software procurement.
- AWS OpsWorks: Configuration management automation, not a software marketplace.

skills: 4.3.6: Understanding the role of AWS Partners (for example, AWS Marketplace, independent software vendors, system integrators).
questions.question:
A financial services company is migrating a complex portfolio of legacy mainframe applications to AWS. The internal IT team lacks experience designing the target architecture and managing the project at this scale. Management wants to engage an external firm with demonstrated AWS expertise to design the migration architecture and oversee implementation.

Which type of AWS Partner would BEST fulfill this role?

choices.text: An AWS Partner Network system integrator, which provides professional services to design, migrate, and implement solutions on AWS using certified architects and project teams
choices.explanation: System integrators in the AWS Partner Network specialize in designing and implementing complex AWS migrations and workloads, providing the architecture and project management expertise needed.

choices.text: An independent software vendor listed on AWS Marketplace, which provides pre-built software products that can be deployed into the customer's AWS account with minimal configuration
choices.explanation: ISVs provide software products; they do not provide professional services for architecture design and migration project management.

choices.text: An AWS Managed Service Provider, which assumes ongoing operational management of existing AWS environments but does not typically lead migration design engagements for new workloads
choices.explanation: AWS Managed Service Providers focus on ongoing operational management of running environments, not designing and leading initial migration projects for legacy workloads.

choices.text: An AWS Distribution Partner, which manages the resale and licensing of AWS services to other businesses and can bundle AWS credits with migration agreements
choices.explanation: Distribution partners handle resale and licensing; they do not provide professional architecture and migration services.

questions.tip: Consider which partner type provides hands-on professional services for designing and implementing complex cloud projects rather than software products or operational management.
questions.explanation:
AWS Partner Network system integrators provide professional services including architecture design, migration planning, and implementation oversight, making them the most suitable choice for a complex mainframe migration.

**Why it works:** System integrators bring certified AWS expertise and project delivery capabilities for large-scale migration and modernization engagements.

**Why the others don't work:**
- ISVs: Provide software products, not professional services.
- Managed Service Providers: Focused on ongoing operations of existing environments, not new migration design.
- Distribution Partners: Handle resale and licensing, not technical professional services.

skills: 4.3.7: Identifying the benefits of being an AWS Partner (for example, partner training and certification, partner events, partner volume discounts).
questions.question:
A cloud consulting firm has recently joined the AWS Partner Network. The firm's leadership wants to understand which financial benefit the APN provides that helps reduce the cost of purchasing AWS services as their practice and customer base grows.

Which benefit of APN membership directly reduces the cost of AWS service consumption for partners?

choices.text: Partner volume discounts, which give APN members access to reduced pricing on AWS services as their usage and tier level increase
choices.explanation: APN partners receive volume discounts on AWS services, enabling lower costs as their AWS usage grows alongside their customer engagements.

choices.text: Access to the AWS Marketplace seller program, which allows partners to list and sell their own software products to AWS customers and earn revenue
choices.explanation: The Marketplace seller program is a revenue opportunity, not a cost reduction on AWS service consumption for the partner.

choices.text: Free access to AWS Enterprise Support for all accounts managed by the partner on behalf of their customers
choices.explanation: APN membership does not include complimentary Enterprise Support; partners and customers must separately purchase support plans.

choices.text: Automatic enrollment in AWS Cost Explorer with enhanced forecasting features that identify savings opportunities across managed accounts
choices.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer is available to all AWS accounts and is not a special APN member benefit; it does not directly reduce service costs.

questions.tip: Focus on the benefit that directly lowers the price partners pay for AWS services rather than tools, programs, or revenue opportunities.
questions.explanation:
APN partners receive volume discounts on AWS services as a direct financial benefit of membership, helping to reduce their costs as their AWS usage scales.

**Why it works:** Volume discounts lower the effective price per unit of AWS consumption for partners, making it a direct cost reduction benefit.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Marketplace seller program: Creates revenue for partners, not a discount on their own AWS costs.
- Enterprise Support: Must be purchased separately; not included with APN membership.
- Cost Explorer: Available to all customers; not an APN-exclusive cost reduction mechanism.

skills: 4.3.7: Identifying the benefits of being an AWS Partner (for example, partner training and certification, partner events, partner volume discounts).
questions.question:
A software company is evaluating whether to formally join the AWS Partner Network. The business development team wants to identify concrete benefits that APN membership provides beyond simply reselling AWS services.

Which TWO benefits does APN membership provide to member organizations?

choices.text: Invitations to AWS partner events, summits, and briefings where partners can learn about upcoming services and network with AWS teams and other partners
choices.explanation: APN partners receive invitations to exclusive partner events and summits, providing access to AWS roadmap information and networking opportunities not available to general customers.

choices.text: Access to AWS partner training and certification programs through AWS Partner Central to help team members build AWS skills and advance partner tier requirements
choices.explanation: APN membership includes access to partner-specific training paths and certification support through Partner Central.

choices.text: Guaranteed placement of the partner's solution in the top search results on AWS Marketplace to maximize customer discovery and sales volume
choices.explanation: APN membership does not guarantee search placement on AWS Marketplace; listing visibility is based on the platform's own ranking algorithms.

choices.text: Complimentary AWS Enterprise Support plans for the partner's own AWS production accounts at no additional charge as part of tier benefits
choices.explanation: Enterprise Support is not included as a complimentary benefit of APN tier membership; partners must purchase their own support plans.

choices.text: Free access to all AWS managed services including Amazon RDS and Amazon EKS at no cost for internal use in building partner-developed solutions
choices.explanation: APN membership does not include free access to managed services; partners consume AWS services at standard or discounted rates depending on their agreements.

questions.tip: Focus on benefits that relate to knowledge, access, and professional development rather than free service entitlements.
questions.explanation:
Two concrete benefits of APN membership are access to partner events and summits, and access to partner training and certification programs through Partner Central.

**Why they work:** Partner events provide strategic access to AWS teams and roadmaps; partner training supports skill-building and tier advancement - both are documented APN member benefits.

**Why the others don't work:**
- Guaranteed Marketplace placement: Not an APN benefit; listing visibility is based on platform algorithms.
- Complimentary Enterprise Support: Must be purchased separately.
- Free managed services: Partners pay for service consumption, potentially with volume discounts but not free access.

skills: 4.3.8: Identifying the key services that AWS Marketplace offers (for example, cost management, governance and entitlement).
questions.question:
The procurement team at a large enterprise wants to ensure that software purchased through AWS Marketplace is deployed only by authorized teams and appears on a centralized AWS invoice for budget tracking. They also need the ability to control which Marketplace products employees can subscribe to across multiple AWS accounts.

Which AWS Marketplace capability addresses governance and procurement control across accounts?

choices.text: AWS Marketplace Procurement System Integration and the AWS Marketplace management features in AWS Organizations, which allow administrators to centrally approve products, restrict subscriptions, and consolidate Marketplace charges into a single invoice
choices.explanation: AWS Marketplace integrates with AWS Organizations to provide centralized governance controls, including subscription approval workflows and consolidated billing, giving administrators control over which products can be purchased across accounts.

choices.text: AWS Service Catalog, which lets administrators create approved product portfolios from AWS-native services and deploy them to end users through a self-service portal within a single account
choices.explanation: AWS Service Catalog manages internally built product portfolios of AWS-native configurations; it does not govern third-party AWS Marketplace subscriptions across organizational accounts.

choices.text: AWS Config rules configured to detect unauthorized software installations on Amazon EC2 instances and trigger automated remediation using AWS Systems Manager
choices.explanation: AWS Config monitors resource configurations for compliance; it does not control Marketplace subscription approvals or consolidate purchasing across accounts.

choices.text: AWS Cost and Usage Reports exported to Amazon S3, which provide line-item visibility into Marketplace charges so finance teams can manually review and approve purchases retroactively
choices.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports provide billing visibility after purchases occur; they do not enable proactive governance or restrict which products employees can subscribe to.

questions.tip: Think about the Marketplace capability that provides proactive control over what can be purchased and by whom, rather than retroactive visibility or post-deployment monitoring.
questions.explanation:
AWS Marketplace provides governance and entitlement features integrated with AWS Organizations, allowing administrators to control which products are available for subscription and consolidate charges for centralized billing oversight.

**Why it works:** Organization-level Marketplace controls give procurement and IT teams proactive authority over software subscriptions across all member accounts.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Service Catalog: Manages internal AWS-native product portfolios, not third-party Marketplace subscriptions.
- AWS Config rules: Post-deployment compliance monitoring, not subscription governance.
- Cost and Usage Reports: Retroactive billing visibility, not proactive subscription control.

skills: 4.3.9: Identifying technical assistance options available at AWS (for example, AWS Professional Services, AWS Solutions Architects).
questions.question:
After reviewing quarterly spending, a startup's CTO realizes the team is overpaying for their AWS environment because the architecture was never optimized after the initial build. Before committing to a redesign, the CTO wants to get no-cost architectural guidance from an AWS resource to identify optimization opportunities and validate their proposed changes.

Which AWS technical assistance option provides complementary architectural guidance to help customers design and optimize solutions at no additional charge?

choices.text: AWS Solutions Architects, who are AWS employees available to customers through sales engagements and events to provide no-cost architectural guidance, best practice recommendations, and solution design support
choices.explanation: AWS Solutions Architects provide complimentary architectural guidance to AWS customers, helping them design well-architected solutions and identify optimization opportunities as part of the customer relationship.

choices.text: AWS Professional Services, which provides a fee-based consulting engagement where AWS experts work on-site or remotely to redesign and implement architectural changes on the customer's behalf
choices.explanation: AWS Professional Services is a paid consulting engagement, not a no-cost advisory resource.

choices.text: AWS Support Engineers accessed through the Business Support plan, who troubleshoot technical issues with existing configurations but do not provide proactive architectural design reviews
choices.explanation: AWS Support Engineers address break-fix technical support cases; architectural guidance and optimization reviews are outside the scope of standard support plan interactions.

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor, which automatically analyzes the account for cost, security, and performance best-practice deviations and recommends specific configuration changes
choices.explanation: Trusted Advisor provides automated checks for specific best-practice deviations; it is a tool, not a human advisor who can validate proposed architectural designs.

questions.tip: Think about which option involves a person employed by AWS who provides guidance as part of the customer engagement model rather than a paid service or automated tool.
questions.explanation:
AWS Solutions Architects are AWS employees who provide no-cost architectural guidance and best practice recommendations to customers as part of the AWS customer relationship.

**Why it works:** Solutions Architects engage with customers to review designs, recommend optimizations, and validate architectural decisions at no additional charge.

**Why the others don't work:**
- AWS Professional Services: Fee-based consulting engagement.
- AWS Support Engineers: Break-fix technical support, not architectural design guidance.
- Trusted Advisor: Automated tool for best-practice checks, not a human architectural advisor.

skills: 4.3.9: Identifying technical assistance options available at AWS (for example, AWS Professional Services, AWS Solutions Architects).
questions.question:
An enterprise is planning a large-scale adoption of AWS across multiple business units and wants to understand the human-led technical assistance options available directly from AWS. The IT governance team wants to identify which resources involve AWS employees providing hands-on or advisory technical help rather than automated tools or third-party firms.

Which TWO options represent AWS-employed technical assistance available directly from AWS?

choices.text: AWS Professional Services, where AWS employees work directly with customer teams on a fee basis to accelerate cloud adoption, design solutions, and implement workloads
choices.explanation: AWS Professional Services is staffed by AWS employees who provide paid hands-on consulting to help customers design and implement cloud solutions.

choices.text: AWS Solutions Architects, who are AWS employees that provide no-cost architectural guidance and design recommendations to customers through sales and engagement channels
choices.explanation: AWS Solutions Architects are AWS employees who offer complimentary architectural advice and best practice guidance as part of the customer relationship.

choices.text: AWS Partner Network system integrators, which are third-party consulting firms that have achieved AWS certification and provide migration and implementation services under their own brand
choices.explanation: APN system integrators are independent third-party firms, not AWS employees; they operate separately from AWS.

choices.text: AWS Marketplace professional services listings, where third-party vendors offer consulting and implementation engagements that can be purchased through the Marketplace catalog
choices.explanation: Marketplace professional services listings are offered by third-party vendors, not AWS employees.

choices.text: AWS Managed Service Providers, which are APN partners that take over ongoing operational management of customer AWS environments on a managed services basis
choices.explanation: AWS Managed Service Providers are APN-certified third-party companies, not AWS employees providing direct technical assistance.

questions.tip: Focus on distinguishing assistance that comes from AWS-employed staff versus certified third-party partners or automated tools.
questions.explanation:
AWS Professional Services and AWS Solutions Architects are both staffed by AWS employees who provide direct technical assistance - one on a fee basis for implementation, the other as complimentary advisory engagement.

**Why they work:** Both options represent humans employed by AWS who engage directly with customers on technical guidance and delivery.

**Why the others don't work:**
- APN system integrators: Third-party firms, not AWS employees.
- Marketplace professional services: Third-party vendor offerings.
- AWS Managed Service Providers: APN-certified partners, not AWS-employed staff.
